### Osteosarcoma Vaccine Study

Now Enrolling Patients​

#### Study Overview 

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of a novel vaccine as compared to standard of care (Carboplatin) following amputation as treatment for canine appendicular osteosarcoma.  

#### Eligibility Criteria 

  * Dog is ≥ 1 year of age 
  * Dog is ≥ 44lbs 
  * Dog is in good general health with the exception of appendicular osteosarcoma 
  * Dog had cytologic and/or histologic confirmation of appendicular osteosarcoma 

#### Study Timeline

  * 6-8 Months 
  * 10-12 clinic visits per patient 

### Interested in this study?
Reach out to a participating hospital to learn more!

#### Ethos Hospitals

Colorado Animal Specialty & Emergency (CASE): Boulder, CO

First Coast Veterinary Specialists & Emergency (FCVS): Jacksonville Beach, FL

Metropolitan Veterinary Hospital: Cleveland, OH

Metropolitan Veterinary Hospital: Akron, OH

Massachusetts Veterinary Referral Hospital (MVRH): Woburn, MA

Mission Veterinary Emergency & Specialty (MVES): Mission, KS

Peak Veterinary Referral Center: Williston, VT

Southeast Veterinary Oncology & Internal Medicine: Orange Park, FL

Veterinary Specialty Hospital – North County: San Marcos, CA 

##### Benefits to Participation 

All study related visits including up to $4000 for amputation are covered at no cost to the pet parent.

## Why does SASH do clinical research?

SASH is committed to providing the best quality care to pets and their owners.

Much like clinical research in human medicine, veterinary clinical research is an essential part of improving future patient care and outcomes. Many of the methods and treatments used at SASH, and other veterinary hospitals, have come from various forms of veterinary research.

Although SASH practices today’s best available veterinary medicine, using the latest equipment, it is also expected that further improvements can be made through continuous research. Through research, we are able to identify the best tests and treatments for our much loved pets.

SASH is the largest veterinary specialist hospital in Australia. We have the combined expertise of around 50 veterinary specialists including neurology, imaging, anaesthesia, critical care and rehabilitation, which are rarely found elsewhere.

# Clinical trial for dogs with splenic haemangiosarcoma

  * Dr Sonya Yu
  * Clinical Research
  * Oncology

### Has your dog recently undergone spleen removal for haemangiosarcoma? Join our clinical trial combining immunotherapy with chemotherapy.

MediPaws is participating in a multi-centre clinical trial, led by the University of Melbourne, investigating a novel treatment approach for dogs with splenic haemangiosarcoma. This study evaluates the use of an autologous tumour vaccine (a personalised vaccine made from your dog’s own tumour) in combination with standard chemotherapy (doxorubicin).

This research has been reviewed and approved by the University of Melbourne Animal Ethics Committee (Project ID 35274).

# Why participate?

### Helping advance treatment for haemangiosarcoma

This study is exploring whether stimulating the immune system alongside chemotherapy can improve outcomes for dogs with this aggressive cancer.
